conventions.convention: The label t counts defects, with 0 ≤ t ≤ n and n−t even; the arc count is (n−t)/2. A link state has no defect inside an arc.
States are diagrams n→t. The right action x·a stacks x above a; diagrams with fewer than t propagating components vanish in the quotient.
Reflection is linear and fixes scalars. The form extracts the identity coefficient from y∘x*, assigning one factor δ per closed loop.
The cellular order is reversed defect order: λ_r dominates λ_t exactly when r ≤ t. Thus strictly greater labels have fewer propagating strands.
The identically-zero-form criterion assumes a nonzero coefficient ring and excludes the empty state: at n=t=0 the form is the unit form.
Simple-module classification is over a field. A zero cell form implies a zero cell-form quotient, without determining the module's actual head.

load_bearing.statement: For a commutative ring R with unit, δ∈R, n≥0 and an allowed t, W_{n,t}(R,δ)=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t), with basis the diagrams having exactly t propagating components.
Over a commutative ring with unit, the diagrams C^t_{x,y}=x*∘y form a cellular basis of TL_n(R,δ), with cell module W_{n,t}(R,δ) and cell form φ_{n,t}.
The reflection-gluing form φ_{n,t} is symmetric and satisfies φ_{n,t}(x·a,y)=φ_{n,t}(x,y·a*) for all module elements x,y and a∈TL_n(R,δ).

Over a field F, the nonzero D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}/rad(φ_{n,t}) are absolutely simple and give all pairwise nonisomorphic simple right TL_n(F,δ)-modules. They are nonzero exactly when the form is not identically zero; in that case its radical is the unique maximal proper submodule.

For n≥1 over a commutative ring with unit, restriction along the rightmost-strand inclusion has the short exact sequence 0→W_{n−1,t−1}→Res W_{n,t}→W_{n−1,t+1}→0, with invalid labels interpreted as zero.

concerns.concern: Step 7.1 says, “Reflection gives the other orientation with q replaced by q^{-1}”. The defined diagram reflection is linear and fixes scalars, so reflection alone does not justify that substitution. The second smoothing branch and its coefficients need to be identified explicitly. The cited Ridout–Saint-Aubin Appendix A, Proposition A.2, equations (A.9)–(A.11), https://arxiv.org/pdf/1204.4505, derives this contribution by expanding the second branch before comparing reflected diagrams. That argument supports the claimed eigenvalue and splitting condition; the local explanation omits this distinction.

seams_checked.note: The link-state constructions preserve the supplier's boundary labels, left-factor-above-right-factor multiplication, loop factor δ, arbitrary commutative-ring scope, and generator relations.

The Gram-determinant proof uses the stated restriction submodule and quotient. The semisimplicity criterion uses the proved cellular datum and nonzero cell-form quotients, preserving the distinction between an identically zero form and a degenerate nonzero form.
